subject: GPU pool runway & autoscale decisions - TorchWave onboarding
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@torchwave.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial capacity preferences for Dedicated onboarding

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Support ticket #TW-882 is open for the onboarding. We're trying to lock down two items before the kick-off: regional choice (US east vs. multi-region) and autoscale/burst policy basics for our first 3-month ramp.

Quick facts:
- Expected steady-state: ~120 concurrent requests at p95 latency target 250ms for the policy-enforced routes.
- Peak test window (first 30 days): 4x steady-state for load tests.
- Data residency: logs and audit data must remain in US only.

Preferred approach from our infra side is single-region initially (us-east) with a controlled burst policy into us-west if we hit sustained CPU/GPU saturation during tests. We also want a short canary (2-hour) auto-fallback to a smaller model variant to keep the UI live for a subset of users.

Can you confirm this is compatible with the SLOs and what minimal pool size we should provision to start? Also, any recommended guardrails to avoid runaway cost during the burst windows?

Thanks,
Samir
Operations Lead, TorchWave

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@torchwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity preferences for Dedicated onboarding

Samir — thanks for the clear summary. High level answers below; detailed provisioning recommendation attached.

TL;DR
- Start with single-region (us-east) as you proposed.
- Provision a conservative pool: 10x the p95 concurrency/worker mapping -> recommend 12 GPUs with planned autoscale to 30 for burst.
- Implement a cost-based burst cap and a token-usage sentinel during load tests to avoid runaway spend.
- Canary policy: yes. We'll configure a 2-hour canary that routes 10% of traffic to a smaller quantized variant and auto-fails back on model-quality triggers.

Attachments: pool-sizing.xlsx (I) — contains the math and tradeoffs.

Immediate next steps:
1) Marissa and Monica will own the activation plan (SOW items + test windows).
2) We need your confirmation on the 12 -> 30 GPU scaling band and whether you want an automatic regional failover to us-west or manual only.
3) We'll draft the SOW and circulation for sign-off (attach SOW draft once we align).

I'll set up a short handoff call tomorrow to lock down the canary metrics.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pool-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@torchwave.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity preferences for Dedicated onboarding

Samir — tagging on operational items and the SOW timeline.

Operational notes:
- Activation sprint: 4 business days to reserve, 3 days to stage images and model artifacts, 1 day for canary. Total runway: 8 business days after signed SOW.
- Autoscale policy we'd apply by default: target CPU/GPU util 60% with smoothing window 5m; scale step size 4 GPUs; cooldown 10m. Burst ceiling at 30 GPUs (manual override if you want higher).
- Cost-guardrails: configure a daily budget alert + hard cap at the burst ceiling. We recommend the initial hard-cap be enforced (not just alerts) for first two test weeks.

SOW draft attached. Please review section 3 (regional constraints and audit log retention) and section 6 (canary success criteria).

Marissa
Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sow-draft.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@torchwave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity preferences for Dedicated onboarding

Thanks — can confirm we accept the 12 -> 30 GPU band and want the hard cap in place for the first 14 days. Two quick asks: 1) can we limit inter-region failover to manual only during the first month?; 2) expose a daily cost estimate feed into our billing team (CSV or Drive link).

Also, for the canary: success = no more than 2% degradation in quality metrics (NDCG for rerank + exact match for classifier) for the 10% sample. If the canary fails, please initiate automated fallback to the quantized variant and open a P1 ticket.

Appreciate the quick turn.
Alex
VP Engineering, TorchWave

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@torchwave.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity preferences for Dedicated onboarding

Alex / Team — noting the decisions and next steps here so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of agreed decisions:
- Region: us-east only for initial activation; manual inter-region failover to us-west (documented runbook).
- Provisioning band: start 12 GPUs, autoscale up to 30 GPUs during bursts; hard cap enforced for first 14 days.
- Autoscale policy: 60% util target, 5m smoothing, step +4 GPUs, cooldown 10m.
- Canary: 2-hour window, 10% traffic to quantized variant; failure triggers automated fallback + P1.
- Data residency: logs and audit data remain in US; retention per SOW (90 days by default).

Action items:
1) Marissa: finalize SOW v0.2 and circulate to Alex for signature (due: EOD Mon).
2) Karthik: populate the activation runbook with pool sizing math and the canary metric thresholds (attach: canary-plan.md).
3) Monica: I'll coordinate the billing CSV feed; expect a test CSV by Monday.

I'll open the onboarding project in Jira and add the timeline items.

Thanks — we'll reconvene after sign-off to schedule the activation sprint.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: canary-plan.md (text)]
